reason: This passage from Exodus 2:16-22 describes Moses in Midian, explicitly portraying him as 'ger' (a stranger/foreigner) in a foreign land ('eretz nokhriyah'). The text focuses on Moses' personal circumstances as a fugitive and his marriage to Zipporah, with no portrayal of the Hebrews as a nation or discussion of their territorial claims. The passage emphasizes Moses' status as an outsider in Midian rather than depicting the Hebrew nation with its own land.
